before: An Effect synchronizes something outside React’s rendered tree. Here the outside value is this sandbox document’s title, not the user’s main browser tab. Derive ordinary JSX directly during render; an Effect is not needed just to calculate a display string.

React.useEffect(setup, [topic]) runs setup after the component commits. React compares each dependency with its previous value using Object.is. The setup reads topic, so topic belongs in the list. Before a changed setup and when removing the component, React calls the cleanup function returned by the previous setup. Here cleanup restores the title captured by that setup. Only one TitleNote owns the title in this example. An empty list would omit this changing input; it is not a way to keep synchronization correct. The frame calls App as the root component with no supplied props. App returns the JSX tree; define it here without calling App() yourself or adding imports/createRoot.

Make the frame title follow topic and restore its prior title when the note is removed. These finite behavior checks do not prove that every possible implementation is correct. Optional local practice: change one input, predict the screen, then run it.
after: An Effect runs work that connects React to something outside its screen description. Here, it changes the preview document's title. It does not change the main CodeQuest tab's title.
The Effect reads `topic`, so `[topic]` tells React when to repeat it. These listed values are called dependencies. React runs the setup after the component has been added or updated on the page.

The returned function is cleanup: work that undoes this setup. React runs it before a changed setup and when removing the note. Here, it restores the previous title. Using `[]` would miss topic changes and leave the title out of date.

Make the title follow topic and restore the earlier title when the note is removed. Keep one TitleNote in charge of this title. Ordinary text shown in JSX can be calculated directly; it does not need an Effect.

before.question: The title setup reads topic but its dependency list is []. After topic changes, which value can become stale?
choices: Both always update because every Effect runs after every render.
The external document title, even though the JSX paragraph rerenders.
The dependency list controls whether setTopic may run.
before.explanation: Dependencies describe reactive values read by the setup. Omitting topic skips its update-driven synchronization; state rendering itself still occurs.

after.question: The Effect reads topic but has `[]`. After topic changes, what can stay out of date?
choices: Nothing, because every Effect repeats after every render.
The document title, while the paragraph shows the new topic.
The dependency list prevents setTopic from running.
after.explanation: The paragraph updates from state. The Effect needs topic in its dependency list to update the outside title too.
